{"Author":"GitHixy","Name":"HitSpark","Punchline":"Replace the game's combat numbers with animated, styleable fly text.","Description":"HitSpark replaces Final Fantasy XIV's combat text with its own renderer: better fonts, tuned motion and real impact on critical hits.

WHAT YOU GET

- Every kind of combat text redrawn: damage dealt and taken, healing, misses and evades, status effects, experience, crafting and loot.
- Eight built-in presets, each a complete look: Classic+, Heroic, Tally, Onslaught, Elemental, Grim, Minimal and Retro.
- Real motion: arcs, fountains, rising and falling paths, scrolling columns, and punch, shake, flash, sparks and trails on crits.
- Multi-hits and damage over time that roll up into one number, with DoT ticks in their own colour.
- Other players' numbers shown smaller, or hidden, for your party and for everyone else, with a distance limit.
- Rear and flank hints for positionals, and an option to let numbers pass under the game's UI.
- A style editor for every category with a live preview, and presets you can share as a short code.

GETTING STARTED

Type /hitspark (or /hs) to open the settings and pick a preset. /hitspark test plays sample numbers on you and your target, even out of combat.
Found a bug or have an idea? Settings > Diagnostics copies a report and opens a GitHub issue for you.

- Relics by job. The Relics area has a By job view and line cards with progress bars. To fill the Armor and GARO frames, update Tales of Milestones to this version and import a new export.
- Societies, currents and collections. Societies show unlock lines and rank bars. Aether currents are listed by zone. Collections are grouped by availability, with Online Store links.
- Settings area. Character, display, and backup and import settings are in one area. The Ledger holds up to 8 characters, and times can show in UTC or local time.
- Themes. The three themes are Lunar night, Crystarium and Light. Expansion tags use the colours of the Lodestone patch notes.
- Jobs meter. The rail has a Jobs meter that adds your combat, crafting and gathering levels, out of 3,330.
- Fix: after an import, the relic row in the list of changes counts relic items. Before, a stage upgrade showed no change, for example "9 to 9"."}

{"Author":"Asteria Nocturna","Name":"Divination.AetheryteLinkInChat","AcceptsFeedback":true,"ApplicableVersion":"any","AssemblyVersion":"7.5.1.0","CategoryTags":["utility"],"Changelog":"e8f691d: Merge pull request #816 from SlashNephy/feat/alic-hunt-journeys

feat(AetheryteLinkInChat): prefer Faloop's starting points for hunt spawn points
74b4951: feat(AetheryteLinkInChat): add exits missing from the game's map markers

The game's map markers do not describe the exit from Yanxia to the
Doman Enclave (The One River): the marker in Yanxia points to the
obsolete map 437, and the current map 463 has no marker back to Yanxia.
So routes through the Doman Enclave were never considered, which is the
Yanxia example in #656.

- Add MapConnections for such exits, starting with Yanxia <-> the Doman
  Enclave. Comparing Faloop's boundary starting points with the game's
  map markers found no other missing exit
- Consider them in the route calculation as ConnectionTeleportPath,
  without counting the distance inside the connected map, as where the
  exit leads to is not known
- Show them like zone boundaries, and stop the Lifestream teleport there

Refs #656

Co-Authored-By: Claude Mythos 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
a3c0a1f: feat(AetheryteLinkInChat): prefer Faloop's starting points for hunt spawn points

Straight-line distance on the map ignores terrain, height and walls, so
the nearest aetheryte is often not the best one to start from.

Faloop's zone data has the spawn points of hunt marks, each with a
journeyPoiId that points to the aetheryte or zone boundary to start
from. Embed them (generated by Scripts/generate_hunt_journeys.py) and,
when a map link is at a known spawn point, only consider the routes that
enter the map at its starting point. Otherwise, fall back to the
straight-line distance as before.

Refs #656

Co-Authored-By: Claude Mythos 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

3cf9a9e: fix(FaloopIntegration): reconnect with a new client after disconnection

After "transport close", SocketIOClient's own reconnection kept the
engine.io session alive (pings continued) but the plugin never received
mob reports again until it was disabled and enabled.

Handle reconnection in the plugin instead, mirroring what re-enabling
the plugin does:

- Disable SocketIOClient's reconnection
- Run a connection loop that logs in again and connects with a new
  Socket.IO client on every disconnection, with exponential backoff
  from 5 seconds up to 5 minutes
- Time out a connection attempt that the server never accepts, since
  ConnectAsync only times out at the transport level
- Stop retrying when the credentials are rejected
- Ignore events from clients that have already been replaced

the nearest aetheryte is often not the best one to start from.

journeyPoiId that points to the aetheryte or zone boundary to start
from. Embed them (generated by Scripts/generate_hunt_journeys.py) and,
when a map link is at a known spawn point, only consider the routes that
enter the map at its starting point. Otherwise, fall back to the
straight-line distance as before.

{"Author":"dajoey","Name":"AutoPotion","ApplicableVersion":"any","AssemblyVersion":"0.2.5.2","CategoryTags":["utility"],"Changelog":"v0.2.5.3 (2026-11-10) [testing]
- Rebuilt against the Dalamud 15.0.4.0 payload for game patch 7.58. No functional changes.

v0.2.5.2 (2026-10-10) [testing]
- **Automatic item uses no longer cancel an open action sequence.** Any potion, ether, deep dungeon medicine or Echo Drops that would land while mudra seals or Ten Chi Jin are held is delayed until the sequence completes, instead of cancelling the ninjutsu mid-chain. The delay lasts only while the sequence is up (a mudra window is about six seconds) and lifts immediately after; at or below 25% HP the heal fires regardless - a cancelled jutsu is cheaper than dying. No other job's behaviour changes.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- With the optional decision log enabled, a held use is recorded with the `heldmudra` near-miss reason, rate-limited like every other near-miss line.

v0.2.5.1 (2026-10-03) [testing]
- **Quick controls for the Lazy Hub window.** The plugin now offers the master switch, "Only in combat", "Only in a duty", the HP, MP and Regen potion switches with their thresholds, and Cure Silence (Echo Drops) to Lazy Hub (`/lazy`) over Dalamud IPC, so they can be changed from one window next to the other lalalazy plugins. Each change does exactly what the matching setting in the plugin's own window does.
- The potion settings apply to the active job's profile, as in the settings window.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Without Lazy Hub installed the plugin behaves exactly as before.

v0.2.5.0 (2026-09-05)

- New per-job option: "Auto-use Echo Drops when silenced". When it is on and Silence lands (mob silence spells, AoE silences, deep dungeon traps), AutoPotion uses Echo Drops from inventory to cure it automatically. Item use is not blocked by Silence, so the cure works exactly when nothing else can.
- OFF by default like every option, and per job like the rest: tick the new box in the settings window for the jobs it should apply to. With it off (the default) nothing changes - not even a status check.
- It reuses the same machinery as the potions: HQ Echo Drops are preferred over normal ones, the shared 750 ms cooldown after any potion use applies, and a Silence that arrives during that cooldown is cured on the next tick.
- If the diagnostic tap is enabled, the cure logs as an `e` event; when it cannot fire the near-miss reasons are `edblocked` (on cooldown / blocked) or `ednostock` (none in the bags).
- No change to potion behaviour. HP/MP/regen thresholds, the overshoot guard, the deep dungeon Rehabilitation lockout and the in-combat / in-duty gates all work exactly as before.

v0.2.4.0 (2026-09-05)

- Added an optional "Log potion decisions" diagnostic, OFF by default. Turn it on with `/autopotion telemetry on` or the new Advanced / Diagnostics section of the settings window, and AutoPotion writes one line to its plugin log every time it uses a potion, plus a rate-limited line when a threshold was crossed and nothing fired.
- Purpose: the log line records the HP%, the MP%, the threshold that was in force and the job, so a threshold can be verified after the fact instead of guessed at. Nothing leaves the machine - the lines only go to the local Dalamud plugin log.
- The "nothing fired" lines say WHY in a short code: `hpover` (a potion was available but the heal would have been wasted), `hpblocked` / `mpblocked` / `rgblocked` (on cooldown or blocked by a status), `hpnostock` / `mpnostock` / `rgnostock` (none left in inventory) and `rgrehab` (Rehabilitation still up in a deep dungeon).
- These lines are heavily rate-limited on purpose: a repeated state logs once, not once per frame. Measured against 214 minutes of real play the near-miss lines come out under one line per minute, so the log stays readable.
- No change to potion behaviour. Thresholds, per-job profiles, the overshoot guard, the deep dungeon Rehabilitation lockout and the in-combat / in-duty gates all work exactly as before, and with the setting off (the default) the plugin does not even build a log line.

v0.2.3.0 (2026-09-05)

- Added the in-game "What's new" popup. After AutoPotion updates, its changelog now opens once inside the game so the changes are visible without a trip to GitHub. It waits until the character is logged in and out of combat, duty, cutscenes and zoning; closing it (Got it, X or Escape) marks it read. Type `/autopotion changelog` any time to reopen it.
- No change to potion behaviour: thresholds, per-job profiles and the in-combat / in-duty gates all work exactly as before.","DalamudApiLevel":15,"Description":"Auto-uses the highest-tier HP potion, MP potion (Ether), and the deep dungeon regen potion (Sustaining / Eurekan / Orthos / Pilgrim's) at configurable thresholds. 3cf9a9e: fix(FaloopIntegration): reconnect with a new client after disconnection

After "transport close", SocketIOClient's own reconnection kept the
engine.io session alive (pings continued) but the plugin never received
mob reports again until it was disabled and enabled.

Handle reconnection in the plugin instead, mirroring what re-enabling
the plugin does:

- Disable SocketIOClient's reconnection
- Run a connection loop that logs in again and connects with a new
  Socket.IO client on every disconnection, with exponential backoff
  from 5 seconds up to 5 minutes
- Time out a connection attempt that the server never accepts, since
  ConnectAsync only times out at the transport level
- Stop retrying when the credentials are rejected
- Ignore events from clients that have already been replaced

Refs #687

d2ea413: feat: use a divination-deploy App token instead of DEPLOY_GITHUB_TOKEN (#799)

reusable-deploy-plugin.yml checks out the distribution repository, opens
a pull request there and merges it. Mint a GitHub App installation token
scoped to that repository instead of using a bot PAT.

Drop the Authorization header when fetching commits.json. This
repository is public so the request needs no authentication, and
expanding a token on the command line exposes it through the process
list.

Reference the reusable workflow by local path. Pinning it by SHA means a
change here does not take effect until every caller is updated, which
would leave a broken intermediate state whenever a secret is renamed.

Drop the explicit create-pull-request author: it defaults to
github.actor, which attributes the deployment to whoever triggered it.

3cf9a9e: fix(FaloopIntegration): reconnect with a new client after disconnection

After "transport close", SocketIOClient's own reconnection kept the
engine.io session alive (pings continued) but the plugin never received
mob reports again until it was disabled and enabled.

Handle reconnection in the plugin instead, mirroring what re-enabling
the plugin does:

- Disable SocketIOClient's reconnection
- Run a connection loop that logs in again and connects with a new
  Socket.IO client on every disconnection, with exponential backoff
  from 5 seconds up to 5 minutes
- Time out a connection attempt that the server never accepts, since
  ConnectAsync only times out at the transport level
- Stop retrying when the credentials are rejected
- Ignore events from clients that have already been replaced

Refs #687

d2ea413: feat: use a divination-deploy App token instead of DEPLOY_GITHUB_TOKEN (#799)

reusable-deploy-plugin.yml checks out the distribution repository, opens
a pull request there and merges it. Mint a GitHub App installation token
scoped to that repository instead of using a bot PAT.

Drop the Authorization header when fetching commits.json. This
repository is public so the request needs no authentication, and
expanding a token on the command line exposes it through the process
list.

Reference the reusable workflow by local path. Pinning it by SHA means a
change here does not take effect until every caller is updated, which
would leave a broken intermediate state whenever a secret is renamed.

Drop the explicit create-pull-request author: it defaults to
github.actor, which attributes the deployment to whoever triggered it.

{"Author":"dajoey","Name":"Gluttony Combo","ApplicableVersion":"any","AssemblyVersion":"1.0.4.324","CategoryTags":null,"Changelog":"v1.0.4.338 (2026-11-10) [testing]
- Rebuilt against the Dalamud 15.0.4.0 payload for game patch 7.58. No functional changes.

v1.0.4.337 (2026-11-09) [testing]
- **The AI decision layer is gone.** The Fight Brain's question side - the raidwide mitigation ask, the pre-pull plan reader (party finder text and the `/gluttony plan` note command), and the party-callout reader - has been removed from the plugin, together with its relay address setting and the two "Plan Reader"/"Callout Reader" switches. GluttonyCombo no longer asks any decision model anything, sends no snapshot anywhere, and keeps no relay URL: the only network path it still uses is the movement tap's `/move/ingest` upload, which records the movement profiles and never carried a decision.
- What stays is pure code and unchanged: the rotation and every combo, the Fight Brain forecast reads and `FB|forecast` lines, the countdown strip, the shadow cast-gate lines, the party-data shadow rules (`FB|party-mit`, `FB|pos-zone`), and the movement recorder and shadow move planner. The move planner's `MP|` decision lines keep their exact format and now always carry the code pick only.
- The shadow move planner no longer has its ask-side toggle; `/gluttony movelog` now switches the recorder and the planner together, and its status line reads two switches instead of three.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.336 (2026-11-09) [testing]
- **Saving a custom action to a hotbar while in PvP now writes the PvP layout.** The custom-action editor's hotbar save told the game the write was a normal-slot write regardless of the current content, so a save made while in PvP updated the regular hotbar set instead of the PvP one; the call now passes the content check (upstream's fix), so the PvP variant of the slot is the one written.
- **The action-replacing hook answers in the game's own yes/no shape.** The IsActionIdReplaceable detour and its delegate declared an unsigned 64-bit return where the game's callback uses a boolean, so the replace decision relied on 0/1 marshalling to land correctly; both signatures now match the native BOOL return (upstream's fix), and the early-return values read true/false instead of 1/0. No behavior change is intended - this removes a latent hook-contract mismatch.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.335 (2026-11-07) [testing]
- **AoE heals no longer fire back to back on a party that is at or near full HP.** Follow-up to 1.0.4.334: on a party whose bars all read full or nearly full, the auto-rotation kept pressing AoE heals - a bar just under 100% never counted as full (regen-tick oscillation and display rounding), and a heal that had just gone out did not stand the press path down while it landed. Two changes, shared by Astrologian, White Mage, Scholar and Sage. First, a member only counts as needing an AoE heal on a real deficit: a bar at or above 98% reads as full for both the one-button average and the auto-rotation's member count, so no threshold setting (including the 100 "disable this check" setting, and a target count of 0, which is now floored at 1) can make a full party eligible. Second, the auto-rotation presses one AoE heal at a time: after a press goes out, the next waits out that cast's flight plus a second for the heal to land and party HP to propagate, so a movement-cancelled cast is no longer re-issued every tick. Real damage is never starved - a party still under the threshold after the window heals again immediately. Single-target heals, raidwide pre-casts and the 1.0.4.334 out-of-range fix are unchanged; the manual one-button still heals when pressed.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.334 (2026-11-07) [testing]
- **Healer one-button AoE heals no longer trigger off party members the heal cannot reach.** The Astrologian, White Mage, Scholar and Sage one-button AoE heal rotations averaged the whole party's HP: a member standing outside the heal's radius kept the average under the threshold, so the rotation kept choosing AoE heals (Helios, Medica, Succor, Prognosis and their oGCD neighbours) that could never heal that member. The trigger now averages only the members inside the heal's own effect radius (15y for the Helios family), alive and targetable, so the rotation returns to damaging while nobody reachable needs healing, and heals again the moment the far member comes back into range. Single-target healing is untouched: a member returning to range is picked up by the single-target path exactly as before. Raidwide pre-casts and the auto-rotation's own cast gate are unchanged.

{"Author":"dajoey","Name":"Gluttony Combo","ApplicableVersion":"any","AssemblyVersion":"1.0.4.324","CategoryTags":null,"Changelog":"v1.0.4.338 (2026-11-10) [testing]

v1.0.4.337 (2026-11-09) [testing]
- **The AI decision layer is gone.** The Fight Brain's question side - the raidwide mitigation ask, the pre-pull plan reader (party finder text and the `/gluttony plan` note command), and the party-callout reader - has been removed from the plugin, together with its relay address setting and the two "Plan Reader"/"Callout Reader" switches. GluttonyCombo no longer asks any decision model anything, sends no snapshot anywhere, and keeps no relay URL: the only network path it still uses is the movement tap's `/move/ingest` upload, which records the movement profiles and never carried a decision.
- What stays is pure code and unchanged: the rotation and every combo, the Fight Brain forecast reads and `FB|forecast` lines, the countdown strip, the shadow cast-gate lines, the party-data shadow rules (`FB|party-mit`, `FB|pos-zone`), and the movement recorder and shadow move planner. v1.0.4.336 (2026-11-09) [testing]
- **Saving a custom action to a hotbar while in PvP now writes the PvP layout.** The custom-action editor's hotbar save told the game the write was a normal-slot write regardless of the current content, so a save made while in PvP updated the regular hotbar set instead of the PvP one; the call now passes the content check (upstream's fix), so the PvP variant of the slot is the one written.
- **The action-replacing hook answers in the game's own yes/no shape.** The IsActionIdReplaceable detour and its delegate declared an unsigned 64-bit return where the game's callback uses a boolean, so the replace decision relied on 0/1 marshalling to land correctly; both signatures now match the native BOOL return (upstream's fix), and the early-return values read true/false instead of 1/0. No behavior change is intended - this removes a latent hook-contract mismatch.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.335 (2026-11-07) [testing]
- **AoE heals no longer fire back to back on a party that is at or near full HP.** Follow-up to 1.0.4.334: on a party whose bars all read full or nearly full, the auto-rotation kept pressing AoE heals - a bar just under 100% never counted as full (regen-tick oscillation and display rounding), and a heal that had just gone out did not stand the press path down while it landed. Two changes, shared by Astrologian, White Mage, Scholar and Sage. First, a member only counts as needing an AoE heal on a real deficit: a bar at or above 98% reads as full for both the one-button average and the auto-rotation's member count, so no threshold setting (including the 100 "disable this check" setting, and a target count of 0, which is now floored at 1) can make a full party eligible. Second, the auto-rotation presses one AoE heal at a time: after a press goes out, the next waits out that cast's flight plus a second for the heal to land and party HP to propagate, so a movement-cancelled cast is no longer re-issued every tick. Real damage is never starved - a party still under the threshold after the window heals again immediately. Single-target heals, raidwide pre-casts and the 1.0.4.334 out-of-range fix are unchanged; the manual one-button still heals when pressed.

v1.0.4.334 (2026-11-07) [testing]
- **Healer one-button AoE heals no longer trigger off party members the heal cannot reach.** The Astrologian, White Mage, Scholar and Sage one-button AoE heal rotations averaged the whole party's HP: a member standing outside the heal's radius kept the average under the threshold, so the rotation kept choosing AoE heals (Helios, Medica, Succor, Prognosis and their oGCD neighbours) that could never heal that member. {"Author":"Valenth Siveria","Name":"I Am Ready","ApplicableVersion":"any","AssemblyVersion":"1.1.0.0","Changelog":"API15 finally","DalamudApiLevel":"15","Description":"# I Am Ready

**I Am Ready** is a Dalamud plugin for Final Fantasy XIV that automatically accepts or declines Party and Alliance Ready Checks based on a customizable counter. 

Whether you are stepping away for a moment or just tired of clicking, this plugin handles ready checks for you while mimicking human reaction times.

## ✨ Features

* **Auto-Answer Ready Checks:** Automatically clicks "Yes" or "No" when a ready check appears.
* **Configurable "Yes" Counter:** Set a specific number of times you want to automatically answer "Yes". Once that limit is reached, the plugin will automatically start answering "No" to prevent pulling when you are actually away.
* **Natural Delay:** Enable a randomized delay (0.7 to 2.5 seconds) before the plugin answers, making it look like a natural human reaction.
* **Smart Chat Triggers (Regex):** Add custom text phrases to the plugin. If someone says one of these phrases in Party or Alliance chat (e.g., "reset", "pulling"), your counter will automatically reset back to zero.
* **Bilingual Support:** The user interface is available in both English and German.

## 🚀 Usage

1. Type `/iar` in the in-game chat to open the configuration window.
2. Click the **Inactive/Active** button at the top to turn the auto-responder on or off.
3. Adjust the **Yes Count** slider. For example, if set to `5`, the plugin will answer "Yes" to the next 5 ready checks, and "No" to any checks after that.
4. Click the **Start** button at any time to manually reset your current counter back to zero.

### Chat Triggers (Regex Patterns)
At the bottom of the window, you can expand the **Regex Patterns** section. Here you can add simple words or complex regex patterns. 
If the plugin reads a matching message in your Party or Cross-World Party chat, it will instantly reset your counter to zero, assuming a new pull or instance is starting!

- Rebuilt against the Dalamud 15.0.4.0 payload for game patch 7.58. No functional changes.

v0.1.7.9 (2026-10-17) [testing]
- **Market-price lookups no longer log warnings while they retry.** When Universalis is slow or busy it answers with a temporary "try again" status or takes longer than before; the price client already retries those on its own with a pause between tries - that is its designed behavior, not a fault, so those lines now go to the debug log. Only one warning is written when a batch gives up entirely after all retries, and stale cached prices are used meanwhile, exactly as before.
- **The price client now waits up to 60 seconds per request instead of 20.** Under load, Universalis sometimes finishes a large price query just after the old 20-second cutoff; the request was cancelled while the server was still working on it and the prices for that batch were refetched from scratch. The longer budget lets those queries land.
- Market-price log lines no longer paste a hundred item numbers into the log; a batch is described as its item count instead.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Full harness: 401/401 PASS (6 new).

v0.1.7.8 (2026-10-07) [testing]
- **Knightshopper no longer buys units that are sitting on a retainer.** The purchase target counted everything the catalog can see, but the fetch-from-retainer step runs after the purchase and brings those units in anyway - with 90 units on a retainer, none in the bags and 9 missing, the run bought 99 instead of 9. The target now counts what is physically in the bags, and the fetch tops the bags up to exactly what the cart needs; every currency routes on the same corrected target.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Full harness: 395/395 PASS (4 new).

v0.1.7.7 (2026-10-07) [testing]
- **Cart dispatches can hand vendor purchases to Knightshopper.** When a dispatch is missing materials that a vendor sells - gil vendors, and currency vendors priced in one currency Knightshopper supports - the run groups that list by currency and buys it through Knightshopper's purchase IPC at target inventory totals, before any shopping stop fires. The run prints each group, its currency and the estimated total cost before anything is spent. Market-board items are never routed, and one attempt per group means a refused purchase never retries; a repeat dispatch asks for the same target totals at most, so nothing is ever bought twice.
- If Knightshopper is missing, busy, refuses LazyCrafter, or has no unlocked vendor for an item, those items fall back to the usual shopping stops - flagged and named in chat exactly as before. Purchases also need LazyCrafter on Knightshopper's allowed-plugins IPC list, which is set in Knightshopper's own settings (IPC permissions); LazyCrafter never changes Knightshopper's settings. The new switch (on by default) is "Buy vendor items through Knightshopper during a dispatch" in the settings.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- With the switch off, or without Knightshopper installed, the run behaves exactly as before.
- Full harness: 391/391 PASS (16 new).

v0.1.7.6 (2026-10-03) [testing]
- **Quick controls for the Lazy Hub window.** The plugin now offers the catalog and price settings (recipes above the character's level, the undersupplied thresholds, the revenue basis, pricing at the home world only, the price refresh interval, the price-match message) and the cart-run hand-off switches (fetching materials from retainers, walking to a summoning bell or to vendors, preferring a currency shop) to Lazy Hub (`/lazy`) over Dalamud IPC, so they can be changed from one window next to the other lalalazy plugins. Each change does exactly what the matching setting in the plugin's own window does.
- The cart-run hand-off switches can only be changed while no cart run is active.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Without Lazy Hub installed the plugin behaves exactly as before.

v0.1.7.5 (2026-09-16)

- **The shopping-stop Resume popup window is gone.** The 0.1.7.4 test pass: the full-screen popup opened at every shopping stop sat over the game and blocked mouse input with the client - verdict: remove the resume extra window. {"Author":"dajoey","Name":"LazyCrucible","ApplicableVersion":"any","AssemblyVersion":"0.1.9.16","CategoryTags":["jobs","utility"],"Changelog":"v0.1.9.17 (2026-11-10) [testing]
- Rebuilt against the Dalamud 15.0.4.0 payload for game patch 7.58. No functional changes.

v0.1.9.16 (2026-10-13) [testing]
- **"Score: three familiars" run-roster mode, off by default.** For score runs. A run roster of one to three familiars scores the Beast Squad III bonus on every board, so with the option on the run roster is the best three familiars for the whole board instead of the board's full roster. The three are chosen from the familiars you own and that are not knocked out: they cover as many of the board's required interrupt, dispel and cleanse needs as any three can, then the damage the board calls to be blunted, then three of one kin when that costs no required cover (the Gambit bonus), then the rest by points. A roster of three saved for a different board is rewritten for the board you enter. Whatever the three cannot answer on the board is named on the window's summary line; nothing pops up. With three or fewer familiars the game registers the battlehorns itself, so the plugin leaves them alone. Found in the settings window and the Lazy Hub as "Score: three familiars".
- With the option off, nothing changes. While AutoDuty drives the run roster the plugin stands by there, option on or off.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v0.1.9.15 (2026-10-13) [testing]
- **Mitigation in the horn picks.** Fights with a damage wall now field a familiar that blunts it, ranked below every interrupt, dispel and cleanse need, and counted only for a familiar above the danger HP line. Durga's Atomic Ray gets a magic answer (drake's Smoldering Scales, pugil's Water Wall or a Scalekin's Scaleskin); Borgny gets coblyn's Vulcanize for the poison plus a magic answer; Gargoyle's Sweeping Evisceration gets a physical answer (a Beastkin's Beastskin, coblyn's Vulcanize or adamantoise's Harden Shell). The fight guide lists these under "Calls for".
- One telemetry line per fight names the team on the horns and the needs it cannot answer (`uncovered=`).
- **Works with AutoDuty.** While AutoDuty runs, it handles the run roster, shop, treasure, spoils and campsite itself, so the plugin stands by there; the battlehorns are AutoDuty's only with its "Fight picks" on, and the plugin picks them otherwise. AutoDuty's active profile is read through AutoDuty's own interface (its config file when that is unavailable), never changed; when neither can be read, every screen stands by, as before. The window shows one quiet line naming the screens it is standing by on.
- **No more corrections on top of AutoDuty's familiar picks.** AutoDuty re-applied its own picks every time, so they never reached a fight.
- **Fight guide: the Snarl -> Parting Blow advice is gone** (Parting Blow no longer dodges a hit since the September 17 hotfix). Plain tankbusters say to let a familiar with enough HP take them under Snarl; poisoning ones (Deadly Thrust, Cold Caress, Toxic Vomit) say to Parting Blow right after the hit so the poison leaves with the familiar; Gargoyle's Sweeping Evisceration says to save the Blink tome for it.
- Item values: Beastly Knife is valued like the elemental axes; Hero's Crown counts its Excellence proc (9 s of nullified attacks); Rapid Recast gear is valued; reraise items are worth a little less at Third Degree.
- **Patch 7.57: battlehorns the game registered itself (teams of three or fewer) are left alone**; a knocked-out member of a three-familiar team is no longer toggled off the horns.
- **Patch 7.57: the board's degree survives a job change** (the game now keeps the Crucible Mode until logout), so the degree passed to Gluttony Combo is no longer reset when the character returns to Beastmaster. It is forgotten at logout.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v0.1.9.14 (2026-10-06) [testing]
- **The board's difficulty degree now reaches Gluttony Combo during a fight.** The degree is set in the lobby (by a click or by AutoDuty) and the character then zones into the duty; the plugin used to forget it at every loading screen, so a fight always read as an unknown degree. It is now kept across loading screens and still forgotten when the Beastmaster job is left or the plugin unloads.

v0.1.9.13 (2026-10-06) [testing]
- **The board's difficulty degree is now read and shared with Gluttony Combo.** The Crucible board layout reports the degree whenever it is set, by a click or by AutoDuty; the plugin keeps the last one (Standard, First, Second or Third) and offers it to Gluttony Combo 1.0.4.288 or newer, which uses it to price the hits a familiar or the character will take. The degree is forgotten when the Beastmaster job is left, and until the first time it is set the plugin reports none. The change is logged as one `PS|` line (`note=degree`).
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.1.9.12 (2026-10-05) [testing]
- **The run-roster need-coverage correction no longer fires while AutoDuty drives the screen.** AutoDuty re-asserts its own roster through a confirm sequence that removes unfamiliar rows one per pass and holds its acceptance until they are gone; every correction written on that surface was removed before entry, and the acceptance follows the build's last pick by about half a second with nothing the plugin can observe in between — a guess there only spent the correction budget on rows that were going to be removed anyway. The surface is now left to AutoDuty entirely. The battlehorn surface is unchanged.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.","DalamudApiLevel":15,"Description":"For the Beastmaster duty Crucible of the Unbroken. Picks are announced in chat. Every automation has its own toggle and manual edits always win. Includes the beast-pick advisor for every board and a read-only recorder that writes each Crucible screen to the Dalamud log. Use /lazycrucible to open.

{"Author":"dajoey","Name":"Lazy Fish Sitter","ApplicableVersion":"any","AssemblyVersion":"0.1.5.1","CategoryTags":["utility"],"Changelog":"v0.1.5.2 (2026-11-10) [testing]
- Rebuilt against the Dalamud 15.0.4.0 payload for game patch 7.58. No functional changes.

v0.1.5.1 (2026-10-03) [testing]
- **Quick controls for the Lazy Hub window.** The plugin now offers the "Sit while fishing" switch to Lazy Hub (`/lazy`) over Dalamud IPC, so they can be changed from one window next to the other lalalazy plugins. Each change does exactly what the matching setting in the plugin's own window does.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Without Lazy Hub installed the plugin behaves exactly as before.

v0.1.5.0 (2026-09-25)

- Persistent seating across fishing hole visits: if the character stands up during a visit to a fishing hole (such as putting the rod away to change bait or use cordials, or manually standing up), the automation now detects the stand and re-seats upon resuming fishing or on the subsequent cast.
- Unaccepted send cap: the 3-send limit per hole visit is now scoped to consecutive unaccepted sends rather than a lifetime cap per hole visit. When a sit is accepted by the game, the counter resets, ensuring long fishing sessions with multiple bait changes or pauses remain seated while still guarding against unbounded retry loops if commands are blocked.

v0.1.4.0 (2026-09-25)

- Sits after a cast: the automated /sit check now runs after a cast once the line is settled in the water (`LineInWater`), in addition to the pre-cast standby beat (`PoleReady`). In active fishing loops or when using automated casting tools, the standby beat between casts typically lasts under a second, which previously prevented the automation from ever triggering across repeated casts (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `IsStandbyBeat`).
- Safe timing: commands are sent only after the line has been in the water for at least 1 second to ensure the cast animation has resolved, and continue to be refused during active casting, biting, hooking, reeling, and position change animations.

v0.1.3.0 (2026-09-05)

- Correction first, because the last release's notes got the game wrong: FFXIV does NOT force standing on every hooked fish. If the character is sitting when the cast starts, the game keeps it seated for the whole loop - a hook may cause a momentary stand, but the game sits back down on its own. v0.1.2.0 was designed around that mistake (one /sit per cast) and this release replaces it entirely.
- Sit once, then stay out of the way. The plugin now sends a single /sit per fishing trip, at a moment the game will actually accept it, and then does nothing for the rest of the trip (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `Decide`).
- That moment is the standby beat: rod out, no line in the water (`FishingEventHandler.State == PoleReady`), held for a second, at least 3 seconds clear of a bite/hook/reel, with the character read as standing for 3 seconds straight. It will never fire mid-cast, with a line in the water, mid-bite, mid-reel, or while already sitting down or standing up (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `IsStandbyBeat`).
- That is why v0.1.1.0 looked like it did nothing: it sent its one /sit the instant the fishing flag came on, which is after the line is already out, and the game swallows the emote there - ten sends across ten sessions, no effect. v0.1.2.0 still counted "line in water" as a valid moment and would have done the same thing.
- No re-sit after every cast, ever. A brief standing read just after a bite, hook, reel or collectable prompt is treated as the game's own animation, not as the character standing up, so the plugin does nothing and lets the game re-seat (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `IsHookish`).
- A "trip" is one visit to a fishing hole, not one cast. The fishing flag drops between casts (v0.1.1.0 saw ten "sessions" in 21 minutes), so the limits are now anchored to the hole and only reset after 20 seconds away from it (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `StartTrip` / `EndTrip`).
- Anti-yo-yo guards, all hard, because a /sit on a seated character STANDS them: never sends while any seated signal reads seated; at least 10 seconds between sends; at most 3 sends per trip with a log line when it stops; and once the game has taken a sit this trip it will not send again unless the seated read has proved it still reports seated with the rod out (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `Decide`, guards 1-5).
- The settings window now shows the trip counters: whether the character is at a hole, sits used out of 3, whether the game took the sit, and whether the seated read works while fishing (file: `ConfigWindow.cs`).
- Removed the "check interval" slider. The plugin now looks every frame, because every limit that matters is a real time limit (10 seconds between sends, 3 seconds of standing before it believes the read, 3 sends a trip) and a 2-second poll just made it step over short standby beats between quick casts. Saved values are ignored, not lost (files: `ConfigWindow.cs`, `Configuration.cs`).
- The policy is now a plain C# class with no game code in it (`Core/SitPolicy.cs`), replayed offline against 26 scripted fishing sessions by `tests/LazyFishSitter.Harness`. Three releases in a row shipped a rule that only broke in game; the harness caught three more before this one shipped, including a dead window that would have stopped a refused /sit from ever being retried.
- Keeps the detailed state logging (every fishing-state and posture change, 40 lines a minute max) and adds a one-line trip summary, so the still-open question - does the game ever report seated while a line is out - can be answered from the log without typing anything in game (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `EndTrip`).

v0.1.2.0 (2026-09-05)

- SUPERSEDED BY v0.1.3.0 AND NEVER FISHED ON: the design premise below was wrong. It claimed the game forces standing on every hooked fish; it does not - if the character was sitting before the hook, the game re-seats automatically. Everything in this entry that follows from that premise (a /sit per stand episode) was removed in v0.1.3.0. Kept here for the record only.
- Re-sat after every cast and every catch, on the mistaken premise above: the unit was a "stand episode" (fishing start, or the fishing state machine passing through Hooking/ReleasingCatch/ConfirmingCollectable), and each episode got at most ONE /sit (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `Arm` / `TrackTransitions`).
- Sent only when it believed the game would accept it: read `EventFramework.Instance()->EventHandlerModule.FishingEventHandler` (FFXIVClientStructs) and required `State` to be `PoleReady` or `LineInWater` for at least 1 s with `ChangingPosition` false. Counting `LineInWater` as acceptable was the second defect - that is exactly where the emote gets swallowed (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `Tick`).
- Proof the sit took: `FishingEventHandler.ChangingPosition` going true within 3 s of the send was logged as `game accepted our sit`, with a 3 s outcome line per send. This part was correct and is kept in v0.1.3.0 (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `TrackTransitions`).
- No detector-driven re-arm: a "not seated" read after a sit never triggered a re-send on its own (that is what yo-yoed v0.1.0.0). Also kept in v0.1.3.0, hardened (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `Tick`).

- **Quick controls for the Lazy Hub window.** The plugin now offers the "Sit while fishing" switch to Lazy Hub (`/lazy`) over Dalamud IPC, so they can be changed from one window next to the other lalalazy plugins. Each change does exactly what the matching setting in the plugin's own window does.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Without Lazy Hub installed the plugin behaves exactly as before.

v0.1.5.0 (2026-09-25)

- Persistent seating across fishing hole visits: if the character stands up during a visit to a fishing hole (such as putting the rod away to change bait or use cordials, or manually standing up), the automation now detects the stand and re-seats upon resuming fishing or on the subsequent cast.
- Unaccepted send cap: the 3-send limit per hole visit is now scoped to consecutive unaccepted sends rather than a lifetime cap per hole visit. When a sit is accepted by the game, the counter resets, ensuring long fishing sessions with multiple bait changes or pauses remain seated while still guarding against unbounded retry loops if commands are blocked.

v0.1.4.0 (2026-09-25)

- Sits after a cast: the automated /sit check now runs after a cast once the line is settled in the water (`LineInWater`), in addition to the pre-cast standby beat (`PoleReady`). In active fishing loops or when using automated casting tools, the standby beat between casts typically lasts under a second, which previously prevented the automation from ever triggering across repeated casts (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `IsStandbyBeat`).
- Safe timing: commands are sent only after the line has been in the water for at least 1 second to ensure the cast animation has resolved, and continue to be refused during active casting, biting, hooking, reeling, and position change animations.

v0.1.3.0 (2026-09-05)

- Correction first, because the last release's notes got the game wrong: FFXIV does NOT force standing on every hooked fish. If the character is sitting when the cast starts, the game keeps it seated for the whole loop - a hook may cause a momentary stand, but the game sits back down on its own. v0.1.2.0 was designed around that mistake (one /sit per cast) and this release replaces it entirely.
- Sit once, then stay out of the way. The plugin now sends a single /sit per fishing trip, at a moment the game will actually accept it, and then does nothing for the rest of the trip (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `Decide`).
- That moment is the standby beat: rod out, no line in the water (`FishingEventHandler.State == PoleReady`), held for a second, at least 3 seconds clear of a bite/hook/reel, with the character read as standing for 3 seconds straight. It will never fire mid-cast, with a line in the water, mid-bite, mid-reel, or while already sitting down or standing up (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `IsStandbyBeat`).
- That is why v0.1.1.0 looked like it did nothing: it sent its one /sit the instant the fishing flag came on, which is after the line is already out, and the game swallows the emote there - ten sends across ten sessions, no effect. v0.1.2.0 still counted "line in water" as a valid moment and would have done the same thing.
- No re-sit after every cast, ever. A brief standing read just after a bite, hook, reel or collectable prompt is treated as the game's own animation, not as the character standing up, so the plugin does nothing and lets the game re-seat (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `IsHookish`).
- A "trip" is one visit to a fishing hole, not one cast. The fishing flag drops between casts (v0.1.1.0 saw ten "sessions" in 21 minutes), so the limits are now anchored to the hole and only reset after 20 seconds away from it (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `StartTrip` / `EndTrip`).
- Anti-yo-yo guards, all hard, because a /sit on a seated character STANDS them: never sends while any seated signal reads seated; at least 10 seconds between sends; at most 3 sends per trip with a log line when it stops; and once the game has taken a sit this trip it will not send again unless the seated read has proved it still reports seated with the rod out (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `Decide`, guards 1-5).
- The settings window now shows the trip counters: whether the character is at a hole, sits used out of 3, whether the game took the sit, and whether the seated read works while fishing (file: `ConfigWindow.cs`).
- Removed the "check interval" slider. The plugin now looks every frame, because every limit that matters is a real time limit (10 seconds between sends, 3 seconds of standing before it believes the read, 3 sends a trip) and a 2-second poll just made it step over short standby beats between quick casts. Saved values are ignored, not lost (files: `ConfigWindow.cs`, `Configuration.cs`).
- The policy is now a plain C# class with no game code in it (`Core/SitPolicy.cs`), replayed offline against 26 scripted fishing sessions by `tests/LazyFishSitter.Harness`. Three releases in a row shipped a rule that only broke in game; the harness caught three more before this one shipped, including a dead window that would have stopped a refused /sit from ever being retried.
- Keeps the detailed state logging (every fishing-state and posture change, 40 lines a minute max) and adds a one-line trip summary, so the still-open question - does the game ever report seated while a line is out - can be answered from the log without typing anything in game (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `EndTrip`).

v0.1.2.0 (2026-09-05)

- SUPERSEDED BY v0.1.3.0 AND NEVER FISHED ON: the design premise below was wrong. It claimed the game forces standing on every hooked fish; it does not - if the character was sitting before the hook, the game re-seats automatically. Everything in this entry that follows from that premise (a /sit per stand episode) was removed in v0.1.3.0. Kept here for the record only.
- Re-sat after every cast and every catch, on the mistaken premise above: the unit was a "stand episode" (fishing start, or the fishing state machine passing through Hooking/ReleasingCatch/ConfirmingCollectable), and each episode got at most ONE /sit (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `Arm` / `TrackTransitions`).

v0.1.4.0 (2026-09-05)

{"Author":"dajoey","Name":"Lazy Market Companion","ApplicableVersion":"any","AssemblyVersion":"0.2.8.17","CategoryTags":["utility"],"Changelog":"v0.2.8.20 (2026-11-10) [testing]
- Rebuilt against the Dalamud 15.0.4.0 payload for game patch 7.58. No functional changes.

v0.2.8.19 (2026-11-10) [testing]
- **Mannequin listings are now detected on clients in any language.** The mannequin check matched a hardcoded English/German/French list of the context menu's "adjust price" label, so on a client in any other language a mannequin listing was never detected and the automation clicked "adjust price" on a mannequin item. The check now compares the menu against the client's own localized Adjust Price label (the fix is ported from upstream Dagobert's Auto Pinch, whose absorbed price formula this plugin already carries).
- **The manual post hotkey now starts from fresh prices.** Opening a retainer's sell dialog while the post hotkey was held kept whatever the previous session had left behind - cached board prices, an in-flight price lookup, per-session gates - so the price written into the dialog could be stale. The session state is now cleared when the sell dialog opens, before the post chain runs (the fix is ported from upstream Dagobert's Auto Pinch).
- **The manual post chain no longer fires from unrelated windows.** The listener behind the post hotkey was registered for every addon opening, so any window that opened while the hotkey was held could queue a manual post chain for a window that was not the retainer sell dialog. It is now scoped to the retainer sell dialog itself (the fix is ported from upstream Dagobert's Auto Pinch).
- Untried build: tested offline against the plugin's offline test suite, not yet in the game.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.2.8.18 (2026-11-09) [testing]
- **Holding the pinch hotkey no longer re-fires the pinch.** The hotkey was read as a level: on every frame the key stayed down the retainer list and sell list draws each re-ran their pinch check, so holding the key queued a new Auto Pinch every drawn frame - and fired again the moment a finished run freed the busy guard. The key is now read as an edge: one press is one fire, and a held key stays quiet until it is released and pressed again (the fix is ported from upstream Dagobert's Auto Pinch, whose absorbed price formula this plugin already carries). Cancelling a run is unchanged: the Cancel button and the /lmc command; the upstream press-again-to-cancel shortcut was deliberately not adopted.
- Untried build: tested offline against the plugin's offline test suite, not yet in the game.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.2.8.17 (2026-11-06) [testing]
- **The overlay buttons no longer have to cover the retainer windows' own controls.** The Auto Pinch, Auto Market and Sweep to Bags buttons are pinned to the top-right corner of the retainer list and retainer sell list windows, where they can cover the venture currency and the windows' close button (reported in issue #12). Each of the three buttons can now be hidden individually under Settings -> Retainers & Hotkeys -> "Retainer window buttons". A hidden button's action stays reachable through the /lmc subcommands, and the Cancel button shown while a run is in progress is never hidden. All three default to shown, so existing settings keep working exactly as before.
- Untried build: tested offline against the plugin's offline test suite, not yet in the game.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.2.8.16 (2026-10-17) [testing]
- **Fresh installs no longer show an import notice for a plugin that was never installed.** A leftover line in the configuration loader set the "imported from Dagobert Price Matcher" flag true on every load that created a new configuration, so a brand-new install showed the import notice and the uninstall hint even though no settings were ever imported. The flag now keeps its false default; a genuine import from a found Dagobert configuration still sets it, and the load log's imported= field reports the real value.
- Untried build: tested offline against the plugin's offline test suite, not yet in the game.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.2.8.15 (2026-10-10) [testing]
- **The Auto-Market panel's two filter dropdowns remember their setting between sessions.** The status filter (every stack / on the list / not on the list / excluded) and the market-category filter used to reset to "every stack, every category" every time the plugin loaded or the game restarted; they now save as soon as they are changed and come back that way. A saved category the current bags do not contain still shows as "every category" instead of silently hiding everything, and the saved choice comes back when the bags hold that category again.

{"Author":"dajoey","Name":"LazyRetainerLive","ApplicableVersion":"any","AssemblyVersion":"0.1.0.2","CategoryTags":["utility"],"Changelog":"v0.1.0.3 (2026-11-10) [testing]
- Rebuilt against the Dalamud 15.0.4.0 payload for game patch 7.58. No functional changes.

v0.1.0.2 (2026-10-03) [testing]
- **Quick controls for the Lazy Hub window.** The plugin now offers the switch that serves retainer data (the port stays in the plugin's own window) to Lazy Hub (`/lazy`) over Dalamud IPC, so they can be changed from one window next to the other lalalazy plugins. Each change does exactly what the matching setting in the plugin's own window does.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Without Lazy Hub installed the plugin behaves exactly as before.

v0.1.0.1 (2026-09-05)


- Corrected a wrong claim in the v0.1.0.0 notes below (and on the mod's web page): **the endpoint does not answer 503 on logout.** Once logged in, it keeps serving that character's last known retainer state - including at the title screen - and only ever answers 503 if it has never read the retainer table at all since the plugin loaded (i.e. it started at the title screen and no login has happened yet). That freeze is deliberate and is the better behaviour: measured previously the frozen live snapshot was still *newer* than AutoRetainer's file, so falling back to the file on logout would have shown the dashboard **older** data, not fresher. No behaviour was changed here - only the description was wrong.
- The settings window no longer reports "serving live snapshot" while logged out. It now distinguishes three states: no snapshot yet, serving a live snapshot, or serving the last-known snapshot while the game is in transition.


- For anything scripting against this endpoint: `readAt` is the time the request was **served**, not the time the data was read from the game, so it does not reveal how stale a frozen snapshot is. Use the settings window (or `/lazyretainerlive debug`) to tell live from frozen.

v0.1.0.0 (2026-09-05)


- First release. LazyRetainerLive reads the logged-in character's LIVE retainer table (the same in-memory data AutoRetainer uses to drive its own countdowns) and serves it as JSON on `http://127.0.0.1:10504/retainers`, so the ffxiv dashboard's retainer panel can show venture countdowns that update the moment a venture is collected instead of whenever AutoRetainer next saves its config file.
- When not logged in (or the live table has no data yet) the endpoint answers HTTP 503, which tells the dashboard relay to fall back to AutoRetainer's file. Loopback only - the port is never reachable from other machines.


- Companion of AutoRetainer - it reads, it never writes, assigns, or collects anything. Settings: Enabled (default on) and loopback port (default 10504). - Added: When GatherBuddy is installed, the Queue and Recipe Tree now display GatherBuddys tooltip on fish and spearfish, including info about the Bait, Time and Weather restrictions and the next uptimes.  
  - Please note that GatherBuddy uses the client language, not Dalamuds UI language like LeveHelper. It's out of my control.

{"Author":"Akari","Name":"Mahjong Advisor","AcceptsFeedback":true,"ApplicableVersion":"any","AssemblyVersion":"0.4.4.0","CanUnloadAsync":false,"CategoryTags":["Utility"],"Changelog":"v0.4.4.0: Chi picker freeze fix. When a call prompt's claimed tile could not be identified, the single-shape chi gate counted shapes for the wrong tile: each candidate offered one run, but the actual tile completed two, so the game opened its shape-selection dialog - which ignores call callbacks - and the match froze (live at South 4 while leading 38,400; bundle 20261030-081345). Chi now fires only when the claim is pinned to one tile, or when every tile that could legally be on offer completes exactly one run; anything else passes instead. The picker-stall warning also logs once rather than every frame. The stale Advisor block that earlier builds wrote into the plugin config is no longer serialised: it was never read, is ignored on load, and disappears at the next config save. An experimental rollout-search re-ranking of discard candidates is included but ships OFF: a 240-match paired simulator A/B (two seeds) rejected it - it traded a 39% relative win-rate drop for nothing - so it stays a foundation for later work. v0.4.3.0: Result-screen retry. The result panel can swallow the first advance callback while it animates; the controller fired it twice and then its acted guard blocked every retry, leaving the screen waiting indefinitely (live Advanced freeze, state 29 unresolved for 12s). Advances now retry every 2.5 seconds while the result state persists, capped at 8 attempts so the deliberately manual match-end screen is not spammed. v0.4.2.0: Match-level tuning. A full hanchan evaluator now plays East+South with real score accounting, dealer rotation, honcha, riichi sticks and placement, and 120 paired matches showed the old risk settings were too passive. Win value 1800 and deal-in cost 4000 beat 1300/5200 on identical deals (average place 2.55 vs 2.65, more firsts, fewer fourths) with the deal-in rate unchanged at 9.3%. A v7 config migration applies the new values. Riichi hand value and placement stance were also tested and left unchanged - both were flat across 60-match arms. v0.4.1.0: Advanced-table defence. Cross-seat genbutsu now uses the pond lengths captured at the instant a riichi marker appears; the old turn-count shortcut broke once calls shortened ponds and could mark a tile discarded before the riichi as safe. Two declared riichi also force a fold for any hand that is not tenpai, overriding the placement chase. The simulator now records the same declaration snapshots: over 1,000 hands the defence fix moved deal-in rate from 10.3% to 9.5% and average points from -22 to +17, while the double-riichi rail was neutral there because the simulation has no placement stance. Live Advanced trial on 0.4.0.0 finished 1st, 4th, then leading when stopped; the 4th lost two deal-ins to one riichi player, the second 12,000 while two were in riichi. v0.4.0.0: Exact scoring core. Completed hands are now scored by yaku, fu, dora and the payment table (closed and open, riichi through yakuman), and the offline simulator uses that scoring for win legality and payouts. Ready-hand valuation was built and benchmarked but stays out of live decisions: over 1,500 simulated hands, mixing exact tenpai values with the existing one-away estimate cut the win rate from 15.4% to 8.1%, so the value scale must be unified for every shanten first. Advice is memoised per table state so the overlay and controller do not recompute the same decision. v0.3.10.0: Silent-endgame defence. The threat model measured a silent opponent as at most 19% likely tenpai, so on a table with no riichi and no melds every safety rule stayed off - the controller pushed one-away hands with 6-9 tiles left to draw into damaten twice in one match (4,200 and 2,200 deal-ins) and paid full tsumo on 14,300 and 20,000 hands. Silent seats now take on a readiness floor that rises from zero at wall 32 to a concrete threat at wall 16, arming the existing late-wall fold and per-tile safety ranking on quiet tables. v0.3.9.0: Chi freeze fixed. The shape-selection dialog ignores scripted call picks (confirmed by the first picker dump), so chi now only fires when exactly one shape is possible - that path completes with no dialog. Multi-shape chi passes instead of stalling; the pass log records how many shapes were declined. v0.3.8.0: Late-wall defence. When an opponent is a concrete threat and the wall is down to the last four go-arounds, the controller folds any hand that is not tenpai instead of pushing a 1-shanten no-riichi hand. This was the 12,000 deal-in in the first match. Diagnostic bundles now also include chi picker dumps. The end-of-match results screen still waits for you by design - that is the one click after a match. v0.3.7.0: Chi is now fully automated. The controller calls chi when the advisor ranks it best, and if the client shows the shape-selection surface it fires the first variant and re-evaluates the hand. The picker layout is dumped once per session to the log folder so shape-specific selection can be refined against real captures. A v6 config migration enables chi. v0.3.6.0: Read each opponent meld strip independently. A hidden empty strip for one quiet seat no longer suppresses every visible meld on the table, so the threat model sees called sets when they exist. This is a readiness/defence accuracy change; automation logic is unchanged. v0.3.5.0: Fix the second freeze. A complete open hand is no longer assumed to be a legal tsumo: the controller checks for an actual yaku and keeps discarding when there is none. Call prompts now prefer the newest board addition over a possibly stale pond tile (the live log claimed 6z/dragon while the actual Pon was 9m), and the log records the last discard tile/seat. A v5 config migration re-enables auto-play/logging. v0.3.4.0: Fix the self-kan freeze. A Kan/Pass bar at state 6 is ignored and the normal discard proceeds instead of firing a Pass callback the client ignores. Session stats are preserved after /mjadv stop so the bundle still shows the run, and a v4 config migration re-enables auto-play/logging for the next launch. v0.3.3.0: Reset the exposed tuning sliders to the fitted win-rate defaults (base hand value 1300, deal-in 5200, noten 1500, opponent hand 4000) with a one-time v3 config migration. Diagnostic bundles now include the actual Dalamud plugin config file from pluginConfigs. v0.3.2.0: State 15 is now treated as the generic other-players state unless real call buttons are present, state 22 (forced riichi discard) is automated, and state 27 (between-hands result/score) is recognised instead of showing stale advice. Overlay/advice are now gated to actual decision states, and diagnostic bundles can read the Dalamud log while it is open. v0.3.1.0: Auto-play and file logging are now on by default, /mjadv session starts a clean logged session, and /mjadv bundle packages the recent JSONL logs, config, layouts, Dalamud log tail and a full last-read snapshot into one zip. Status changes are now logged as auto-status records. v0.3.0.1: Re-arm auto-play on a state change even when the hand happens to repeat, and wait for the Riichi/Pass prompt to close before cutting the riichi tile. v0.3.0.0: Optional auto-play. Replays the client's FireCallback protocol for discards, calls, riichi, ron/tsumo and result advancement, using the reference solver's live-verified handshake and timing guards. Off by default; /mjadv auto [on/off] or /mjadv stop toggles it. Pon/ron/tsumo/riichi are enabled by default, chi and kan are opt-in, the chi shape picker pauses for a manual choice, and the new-hand screen is never auto-advanced. Added /mjadv hand and /mjadv options diagnostics. v0.2.0.2: Keep the previous wall count, so the wall-jump half of new-hand detection actually fires. v0.2.0.1: Reset the pond baselines at the start of a new hand, so the first discard of the hand is tracked and the first call prompt gets the right claimed tile. v0.2.0.0: Meld containers now read by default (112-115 families), with a fail-closed check against our own called-meld count. Own meld tiles are recovered from hand deltas when nodes are unavailable, so ukeire no longer counts tiles already in a call. Riichi detection is marker-node only; the dead rotation and score-drop paths are gone. One node-tree walk per read instead of up to seven. Fixed dead hands getting a nonzero win rate and Pass inventing a yaku path. Red-five decoding accepts both absolute and alias ids. Removed the obsolete fold-threshold setting. Setup window no longer reopens every launch. Added /mjadv melds diagnostics and richer log records.","DalamudApiLevel":15,"Description":"Reads your Doman Mahjong hand, discards, dora, scores and called melds, then ranks each discard by hand speed against deal-in risk. Auto-play and file logging are on by default in this build: sit at a casual table and it plays, then /mjadv bundle packages the logs for support. /mjadv stop or the Automation tab returns to manual suggestions instantly. Discard piles and meld strips are found automatically; the node tools are only a fallback.\nhttps://raw.githubusercontent.com/dexcss/DalamudPlugins/main/repo.json","DownloadLinkInstall":"https://github.com/dexcss/MahjongAdvisor/releases/latest/download/MahjongAdvisor.zip","DownloadLinkTesting":"https://github.com/dexcss/MahjongAdvisor/releases/latest/download/MahjongAdvisor.zip","DownloadLinkUpdate":"https://github.com/dexcss/MahjongAdvisor/releases/latest/download/MahjongAdvisor.zip","InternalName":"Mahjong.Advisor.Plugin","IsTestingExclusive":false,"LoadPriority":0,"LoadRequiredState":0,"LoadSync":false,"MinimumDalamudVersion":null,"Punchline":"Discard advice and optional auto-play for Doman Mahjong.","RepoUrl":"https://github.com/dexcss/MahjongAdvisor","Tags":["mahjong","doman","gold-saucer","auto-play","advisor"],"TestingAssemblyVersion":"0.4.4.0","TestingDalamudApiLevel":15}

{"Author":"dajoey","Name":"PvP Solver","ApplicableVersion":"any","AssemblyVersion":"0.1.1.2","CategoryTags":null,"Changelog":"v0.1.2.14 (2026-11-10) [testing]
- Rebuilt against the Dalamud 15.0.4.0 payload for game patch 7.58. No functional changes.


- **Removed the AI decision layer.** The optional relayed decision model (focus picking, Limit Break firing and the healer-call shadow lines, with their "call the shots" settings row and its relay address field) is gone from the plugin. No fight snapshot is built or sent anywhere anymore, and the plugin makes no decision calls of any kind.
- Targeting, Guard, Recuperate, the defensive table, StickyTarget and every other rotation behavior are unchanged. The defensive rules keep reading real HP (current HP out of the maximum) under the neutral name `RealHp.HpRatio`; no threshold or default moved.
- PvP Solver still never moves the character and never fires a PvP Limit Break on its own logic, exactly as before.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.


- **The Jev co-pilot logs the plain code rule's answer beside Jev's, for both of its questions.** Each `JV|focus-pick` line names the enemy Jev picked and the enemy the plain rule would pick (the lowest-HP enemy in attack range); each `JV|lb-shadow` line names Jev's Limit Break call and the code rule's. Both answers are recorded side by side and graded after the session, to show which one decides better. Log only: targeting, Limit Break firing and every other behavior are unchanged.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.


- Upstream engine sync (RotationSolverReborn a560469db): the rotation engine now builds in upstream's merged single-project layout.
- Ports upstream engine fixes: the action manager is read at call time instead of a pointer cached at startup (a stale-pointer crash class), configuration saves are atomic (write to a temp file, then replace), and the shield-value calculation can no longer overflow on very large HP values.
- No rotation behavior change; the 21 PvP rotations and their presets are untouched.

v0.1.2.10 (2026-11-01) [testing]
- **The per-job defensive actions also read real HP.** Heart of Corundum, Tempera Coat, Earth's Reply, Riddle of Earth, the Bloodbath rows, Lady of Crowns, Microcosmos, Meisui, Impalement, Xenoglossy's low-HP arm and Shadowbringer's HP arm compared their "use below this HP" thresholds against predicted HP, which counts heals still on the way; predicted can read 84% one second before a death at about 40% real HP. They now compare against the current HP out of the maximum, the same real value Guard and the defensive table already use. Thresholds and defaults are unchanged, and reads of enemies' and allies' HP (Smite, Guardian, Blasting Zone, Perfectio, the burst target) are untouched.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v0.1.2.9 (2026-11-01) [testing]
- **Self-defence now reads real HP.** Guard, Recuperate and the generic defensive actions (the "use below X% HP" table) compared their thresholds against predicted HP, which counts heals still on the way; predicted can read 84% one second before a death at about 40% real HP, so nothing fired. All of them now compare against the current HP out of the maximum, the same real value the Jev snapshot uses. Thresholds and defaults are unchanged.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v0.1.2.8 (2026-10-31) [testing]
- **"Let Jev call the shots" now sees real HP.** The player's and allies' HP sent to Jev is the current HP out of the maximum, no longer PvP Solver's predicted HP, which counts heals still on the way. In one match Jev was told 84% one second before a death at about 40%.
- **Jev's pick no longer drops when Jev is briefly unsure.** The relay now keeps the last pick itself while that enemy is still hittable, and drops it on purpose when the enemy goes under Guard, out of reach or stale. PvP Solver follows the relay's call and never brings a dropped pick back. Only with an older relay does PvP Solver keep the last pick, for up to three seconds after Jev gave it, while that enemy is still a valid target.
- **The Limit Break log matches what happened.** `JV|lb-fired` is written once when the Limit Break goes off in a fire window. `JV|lb-fire-skip` is written only when a window closes without it, with the reason: unusable, follow-up, out-of-range, no-target or timeout. A report of the use that arrives up to two seconds late still counts as fired. Before, a skip line could appear in windows that then fired, and windows that really failed wrote nothing.
- **Each action used is reported once.** The game reports each action twice; the same action on the same target within 1.5 seconds now counts once in the snapshot.

- Eat buttons on the Bonuses tab. Each meal in your inventory has an Eat button. One click eats one meal. The button is not available when the game refuses the meal.
- Eat button in /tm food. The food window has the same button for a meal that is in your inventory.

- New layout. Next Steps is the first screen. It shows 5 cards for what to do next, and "Show 5 more" shows 10. Daily, Weekly and Seasonal rows are below it in the rail. The header shows the area title, the age of your data and 4 clocks.
- Challenge Log. Each Challenge Log entry has its own row, with links and typed counts. Suggested and Completed groups are included.
- Routine sub-checks. A routine can have its own boxes: one for each roulette, a Tank You pick, 12 allied society boxes and Grand Company chips. "Edit routines" changes the rows.
- Relics by job. The Relics area has a By job view and line cards with progress bars. To fill the Armor and GARO frames, update Tales of Milestones to this version and import a new export.
- Societies, currents and collections. Societies show unlock lines and rank bars. Aether currents are listed by zone. Collections are grouped by availability, with Online Store links.
- Settings area. Character, display, and backup and import settings are in one area. The Ledger holds up to 8 characters, and times can show in UTC or local time.
- Themes. The three themes are Lunar night, Crystarium and Light. Expansion tags use the colours of the Lodestone patch notes.
- Jobs meter. The rail has a Jobs meter that adds your combat, crafting and gathering levels, out of 3,330.
- Fix: after an import, the relic row in the list of changes counts relic items. Before, a stage upgrade showed no change, for example "9 to 9".","SourceRepo":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LegendsOfTheGame/TimeMemoriaV3/main/repo.json"}

- Fix: the plugin no longer writes its settings file every 5 seconds while Cosmic Exploration data is loaded. It writes the file only when a tool's progress changes.
- Fix: the job list on the Progression tab no longer scrolls past its end.
- KamiToolKit is updated to its current version.
Adventurer's Ledger (Pandora Lunar):
- New layout. Next Steps is the first screen. It shows 5 cards for what to do next, and "Show 5 more" shows 10. Daily, Weekly and Seasonal rows are below it in the rail. The header shows the area title, the age of your data and 4 clocks.
- Challenge Log. Each Challenge Log entry has its own row, with links and typed counts. Suggested and Completed groups are included.
- Routine sub-checks. A routine can have its own boxes: one for each roulette, a Tank You pick, 12 allied society boxes and Grand Company chips. "Edit routines" changes the rows.
- Relics by job. The Relics area has a By job view and line cards with progress bars. To fill the Armor and GARO frames, update Tales of Milestones to this version and import a new export.
- Societies, currents and collections. Societies show unlock lines and rank bars. Aether currents are listed by zone. Collections are grouped by availability, with Online Store links.
- Settings area. Character, display, and backup and import settings are in one area. The Ledger holds up to 8 characters, and times can show in UTC or local time.
- Themes. The three themes are Lunar night, Crystarium and Light. Expansion tags use the colours of the Lodestone patch notes.
- Jobs meter. The rail has a Jobs meter that adds your combat, crafting and gathering levels, out of 3,330.
